unit_result_entry.title: Function fields turn parts of the random-matrix dictionary into theorems
unit_result_entry.why_material: A structurally related setting where RH is known lets Katz-Sarnak prove random-matrix predictions, offering exact analogue evidence without transferring those proofs automatically to number fields.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: The survey states the analogy broadly and does not specify the individual function-field theorems.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Random matrices predict the full hierarchy of zeta moments and are calibrated by known cases
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Known first and second moments establish anchors, matrix size near log(T/2pi) supplies the translation, and Keating-Snaith values extend the coefficient pattern to all moments while analytic special cases and high-zero computations test the dictionary.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Iterated logarithms can make divergent behavior look bounded on every feasible computation
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The warning explains a concrete mechanism behind false computational conjectures: asymptotically unbounded functions such as iterated logarithms can remain visually flat, so numerics need theoretical or heuristic support.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: After normalizing local density, zeta zeros match random Hermitian eigenvalue statistics; the dictionary predicts spacing and moment laws, high-zero computations calibrate them, and function fields prove related predictions in a tractable analogue.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: Statistical agreement and function-field theorems do not prove the number-field dictionary or RH.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Unfolded zero statistics support a random-matrix conjecture engine with an analogue check
